page: Amazon Web Services c6gd.2xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by an AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor. Built on the arm64 architecture, this instance features 8 physical cores and 8 vCPUs with a dedicated allocation, running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. For local storage, the instance includes a bundled 474 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps, managed via the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average performance across core compute and memory operations, alongside some limitations in specialized workloads. The instance achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1519.88 and a multi-core score of 12133.14, both falling within the average range. Memory bandwidth is measured at 473.11 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 116.89 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. However, single-threaded performance shows weaknesses, with a Geekbench single-core score of 930.0 and a gzip compression rate of 20.32 GB/sec. Cryptographic and decompression tasks also register in the lower tiers, as evidenced by a Passmark encryption score of 1084.81 and a bzip3 single-threaded decompression speed of 6.93 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c6gd.2xlarge leverages the ARMv8 architecture to deliver balanced compute performance per resource unit, complemented by high-speed local NVMe storage. This hardware profile is well-suited for workloads requiring a combination of dedicated compute resources and fast local storage, such as database operations, static web serving, and software compilation. It is less optimal for heavy single-threaded processing or large-scale LLM inference, where text generation speeds for a 7B model drop to 6.75 tokens/sec. Appropriate workloads include Redis deployments, web serving, and general-purpose database tasks.
